prospects.name: Jeremiah Smith
prospects.blurb: The unanimous 1.01. Every list we checked has him first, PFF calls him generational and DLF's superflex mock takes him over every QB. Through Ohio State's first stretch he has 44 catches, 823 yards and 9 TDs (WalterFootball). Draft Sharks compares him to early-career Julio Jones.

prospects.name: Cam Coleman
prospects.blurb: Still a first-round talent (15th in the Tankathon and CBS mocks), but the production hasn't matched the hype: about 20 catches for 334 yards and 6 TDs in seven games after transferring from Auburn, slowed by a tailbone injury and uneven QB play. He's a red-zone threat with big-play tools. Volume is the question.

prospects.name: Darian Mensah
prospects.blurb: The steadiest QB riser. He's a top-six pick in the Tankathon, CBS and A to Z mocks and third on NFL Draft Buzz's board. He's accurate, handles pressure and throws to all three levels. In superflex he's now in the QB1–QB2 conversation with Mestemaker.

prospects.name: Jadan Baugh
prospects.blurb: The biggest RB riser. He has 600 yards at 7.2 YPC and a nation-leading 11 TDs through four games, and B/R calls him the most complete back on its board. The one knock is receiving: just 18 yards so far after Draft Sharks praised his hands last year.

prospects.name: Charlie Becker
prospects.blurb: A big outside X receiver and former track athlete who wins contested catches. He sat behind Omar Cooper and Elijah Sarratt in 2025, and now has 27 catches, 477 yards and 8 TDs (WalterFootball). Dynasty Nerds compares him to Alec Pierce, and Draft Sharks has him as the WR3.

prospects.name: Kewan Lacy
prospects.blurb: The best PPR back in the class for most dynasty sites. He ran for 1,567 yards and 24 TDs as a first-year starter and has a true three-down skill set. A shoulder injury cost him time in September (4.9 YPC, 4 TD), but Dynasty Nerds still has him at RB1.

prospects.name: Arch Manning
prospects.blurb: Still the biggest name and highest ceiling, but his stock has fallen. He's out of the first round in the latest CBS, Tankathon and A to Z mocks after an uneven season, and there was benching talk after a rough game. Dynasty boards still rank him top five on upside. If he stays for 2027, his price could keep dropping.
prospects.status_note: Has slid out of first-round mocks after an uneven season, with benching talk after a rough game.

prospects.name: Drew Mestemaker
prospects.blurb: The QB1 in NFL mocks right now. Tankathon, Field Yates and CBS all have him going No. 1 or 2 overall, and A to Z has him fourth. He has the best arm in the class, outdueled Dante Moore in the upset of Oregon, and PFF graded him at 88.0 through five games (91.4 from a clean pocket). Dynasty boards still lag: most were set before his October run.

prospects.name: Jamari Johnson
prospects.blurb: The TE1 on most boards, and B/R has him No. 6 overall as the most versatile, pro-ready tight end. At 6'5" and 255 he outplayed Kenyon Sadiq late in 2025. He's back from an early injury. A strong fit for our TE premium.

prospects.name: Dante Moore
prospects.blurb: The top QB on preseason superflex boards, but head injuries have derailed his season: a concussion against USC in Week 4, then ruled out again for Nebraska on Oct. 17 as Dylan Raiola started. He's an accurate pocket passer when healthy. NFL mocks now range from 13th (Tankathon) to 30th (CBS), and whether he declares is uncertain.
prospects.status_note: Concussion against USC in Week 4, then ruled out again for Nebraska on Oct. 17. Repeated head injuries and a possible return or transfer cloud his 2027 status.

prospects.name: CJ Carr
prospects.blurb: Field Yates mocks him seventh and Tankathon 12th. He's the most pro-ready passer in a pro-style offense, with a strong TD-to-INT ratio. Dynasty boards still have him late in round 1 or early round 2, so he's a value if the NFL buzz holds.

prospects.name: Trey'Dez Green
prospects.blurb: A basketball-sized red-zone weapon with rare speed. A Week 3 knee injury has him out until roughly Week 10 (WalterFootball), and B/R flags durability. Hands and routes still need work (TSN). He's a high-upside TE2 in a TE-premium league.

prospects.name: Trinidad Chambliss
prospects.blurb: A first-round QB in most current mocks (5th A to Z, 9th Field Yates, 22nd CBS, 27th Tankathon) and Draft Sharks' superflex QB2 earlier this month. He's a mobile gamer with a strong arm. Size is the main question.

prospects.name: Nick Marsh
prospects.blurb: A physical Michigan State transfer with strong yards after the catch and good footwork for his size. Dynasty Nerds uses an A.J. Brown comp. He's the clear No. 2 behind Becker in Indiana's passing game.

prospects.name: KJ Duff
prospects.blurb: A 6'6", 225-pound contested-catch target with 33 catches for 628 yards and 7 TDs (fourth nationally at one point). Draft Sharks loves the size and production, but separation and route consistency (TSN) are real questions for the NFL.

prospects.name: Ryan Coleman-Williams
prospects.blurb: Elite after the catch and also a punt returner. Drops dropped him from first-round talk, but he's caught 17 of 24 targets with one drop this year (FTN). If his hands stay clean, he climbs.

prospects.name: Ahmad Hardy
prospects.blurb: The best pure power back in the class. He's an All-American recovering from a May gunshot wound to the upper leg, and Missouri targeted a mid-September return. Draft Sharks notes limited receiving work, and FTN raises the chance he returns to school if his season gets cut short.

prospects.name: LaNorris Sellers
prospects.blurb: The best dual-threat QB in the class, with a huge arm and real rushing upside. Draft Sharks sees top-five fantasy potential if he starts. His 2026 decision-making has been rough (3 TD, 3 INT in two SEC losses), and FTN suggests he might return to school. He's the boom-or-bust superflex QB of the class.

prospects.name: Jayden Maiava
prospects.blurb: He led the nation in passing early (1,499 yards, 14 TD). He has the size teams want, though FTN calls his arm less than ideal.

prospects.name: Mark Fletcher
prospects.blurb: A big, physical back whom Draft Sharks projects as a Day 2 NFL pick. He's a solid RB2 type for rookie drafts.

prospects.name: Reed Harris
prospects.blurb: The breakout of September. He's 6'5" and 220 with 374 yards and 5 TDs in his first three games. Draft Sharks floats him as a possible first-round NFL pick.

prospects.name: Nate Frazier
prospects.blurb: An efficient, bruising Georgia back. Dynasty Nerds sees a Day 2 pick but wants more passing-game work.

prospects.name: Bryant Wesco
prospects.blurb: A fast outside receiver who does damage after the catch. He has a Day 2 NFL profile and is a solid second-round rookie pick.

prospects.name: Julian Sayin
prospects.blurb: Out indefinitely after hurting his throwing arm against Indiana on Oct. 17, and Ohio State is preparing for him to miss the rest of the regular season. Before that he was an accurate, quick-processing passer with questions about arm strength and frame. With the injury, a return to school for the 2028 draft looks likely.
prospects.status_note: Injured his throwing arm late in the Oct. 17 win over Indiana. Ohio State is preparing for him to miss the rest of the regular season, and he may return to school for the 2028 draft.

prospects.name: LJ Martin
prospects.blurb: A dependable, every-down BYU back with a Day 2 projection from Draft Sharks.

prospects.name: Mario Craver
prospects.blurb: A twitchy, undersized Texas A&M receiver who wins with quickness. He's a mid-second-round type.

prospects.name: Ryan Wingo
prospects.blurb: An explosive athlete who could test his way up at the combine. He's playing second fiddle to Cam Coleman for now.

prospects.name: Duce Robinson
prospects.blurb: A former five-star TE-sized receiver at 6'6" who's still putting it together.

prospects.name: Justice Haynes
prospects.blurb: A former five-star who's been productive since leaving Alabama. TWSN likes him more than Draft Sharks does.

prospects.name: Isaac Brown
prospects.blurb: An explosive, home-run-hitting back whose 2026 start has been slow (4.1 YPC, under 3.0 in two games). His value rises if Louisville uses him more as a receiver.

prospects.name: TJ Moore
prospects.blurb: Draft Sharks has him much higher in 1QB (11th) than in superflex. He's a long Clemson receiver with upside.

prospects.name: Brendan Sorsby
prospects.blurb: His film is impressive, but gambling-related ineligibility will cost him a season, and Draft Sharks sees a Day 2–3 NFL slide.

prospects.name: Omarion Miller
prospects.blurb: A big receiver held back by poor QB play. Dynasty Nerds thinks a strong Senior Bowl could lift him.

prospects.name: Hollywood Smothers
prospects.blurb: B/R's RB4. He's a quick, elusive back who shares work in Austin.

prospects.name: Deuce Alexander
prospects.blurb: B/R loves him (No. 20 overall), citing elite speed, crisp routes and a Garrett Wilson comparison. Dynasty boards haven't caught up yet.

prospects.name: Antwan Raymond
prospects.blurb: A productive Big Ten back whom Draft Sharks also sees as a possible Day 2 pick.

prospects.name: Isaiah Sategna III
prospects.blurb: A speedy Oklahoma playmaker in the WR4–5 range on Draft Sharks' boards.

prospects.name: Cameron Dickey
prospects.blurb: A productive Texas Tech back. Draft Sharks has him in the RB7 range.

prospects.name: Nico Iamaleava
prospects.blurb: A former five-star with a live arm who's rebuilding his stock at UCLA. He's a superflex dart.

prospects.name: Raleek Brown
prospects.blurb: A small, explosive back in a committee at Texas. He's a change-of-pace type.

prospects.name: Terrance Carter
prospects.blurb: A receiving TE with big Big 12 production.

prospects.name: Fluff Bothwell
prospects.blurb: A powerful Mississippi State back who's a fourth-round flier.

prospects.name: Wayne Knight
prospects.blurb: A smaller, shifty UCLA back who catches the ball.

prospects.name: DJ Vonnahme
prospects.blurb: Draft Sharks calls him a potential top TE prospect. He's a good TE-premium dart in round 3.

prospects.name: Amare Thomas
prospects.blurb: Houston's go-to receiver, a productive Group of Five type.

prospects.name: Cam Cook
prospects.blurb: A high-volume transfer back for West Virginia.

prospects.name: Eugene Wilson III
prospects.blurb: A quick slot receiver who's healthy again at LSU after injury-hit years at Florida.

prospects.name: Nyck Harbor
prospects.blurb: Maybe the best athlete in college football, but the receiving production still hasn't come (Dynasty Nerds).

prospects.name: Rocky Beers
prospects.blurb: A big-bodied Oklahoma TE who's a late-round TE-premium stash.

prospects.name: Wyatt Young
prospects.blurb: TSN likes him as an explosive big slot with reliable hands and a full route tree.

prospects.name: Luke Reynolds
prospects.blurb: WalterFootball ranks him 39th overall. He's a well-rounded TE who could go top-75 in the NFL draft.

prospects.name: CJ Baxter
prospects.blurb: A former Texas back rebuilding his stock at Kentucky after injuries.

prospects.name: Eric Singleton Jr.
prospects.blurb: A speed receiver who has moved around the SEC.

prospects.name: DeSean Bishop
prospects.blurb: A compact, explosive Tennessee back.

prospects.name: Benjamin Brahmer
prospects.blurb: A 6'6" Penn State TE with NFL size. He's a fourth-round TE-premium stash.

prospects.name: Cooper Barkate
prospects.blurb: A Duke transfer who's catching passes from Mensah at Miami.

prospects.name: Austin Simmons
prospects.blurb: The fastest-rising QB of October. CBS mocks him second overall and Tankathon early in round 2. He's a big, strong-armed pocket passer who transferred from Ole Miss, and he threw for 340 yards on 23 of 30 against Florida. Dynasty boards haven't added him yet, so he's a superflex sleeper with real draft-capital upside.

prospects.name: Jayce Brown
prospects.blurb: A transfer receiver in LSU's rotation.

prospects.name: DJ Lagway
prospects.blurb: A former five-star rebuilding at Baylor. TWSN has him in the top 25.

prospects.name: Danny Scudero
prospects.blurb: A productive slot receiver who followed Coach Prime's system to Colorado.

prospects.name: Sam Leavitt
prospects.blurb: A mobile transfer QB. WalterFootball has him 42nd overall.

prospects.name: Dylan Raiola
prospects.blurb: He's starting for Oregon while Moore is out. Draft Sharks thinks he could play his way into first-round NFL talk.

prospects.name: Aneyas Williams
prospects.blurb: A former top recruit stuck behind a deep Notre Dame backfield.

prospects.name: Dorian Thomas
prospects.blurb: A receiving TE at Cal on Draft Sharks' radar.

prospects.name: Jordan Faison
prospects.blurb: TSN (No. 37 overall) sees an ace slot receiver. Dynasty boards have him much lower.

prospects.name: CJ Bailey
prospects.blurb: A young NC State starter with real arm talent.

prospects.name: Isaiah Horton
prospects.blurb: A big-bodied outside receiver at Texas A&M.

prospects.name: Waymond Jordan
prospects.blurb: A JUCO transfer who has carved out a role at USC.

prospects.name: Luke Hasz
prospects.blurb: A former Arkansas TE whose career has been injury-hit.

prospects.name: Drake Lindsey
prospects.blurb: TSN's surprise top-50 QB, who needs to put arm, accuracy and athleticism together.

prospects.name: Decker DeGraaf
prospects.blurb: An athletic Washington TE.

prospects.name: Mike Matthews
prospects.blurb: A former five-star WR now at Tennessee.

prospects.name: Caleb Odom
prospects.blurb: A 6'5" receiver-turned-TE with mismatch size.

prospects.name: Cam Edwards
prospects.blurb: A Michigan State back on the deep-sleeper list.

prospects.name: Lawson Luckie
prospects.blurb: A Georgia TE who's been waiting his turn.

prospects.name: Braylon Staley
prospects.blurb: A quick Tennessee receiver.

prospects.name: Brett Norfleet
prospects.blurb: A blocking-first Missouri TE with some receiving upside.

prospects.name: Kenny Johnson

prospects.name: Evan Stewart
prospects.blurb: A former five-star with elite speed whose production never matched the hype.
